package_info.package_name: MageCart web skimming script (injected via Picreel)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (JavaScript injected via third-party web marketing service)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (all sites integrating compromised Picreel code)
package_info.why_malicious: The MageCart script is malicious because it is injected into legitimate websites via a compromised third-party supplier (Picreel) and is designed to steal payment data from users by skimming sensitive information from web forms. This results in unauthorized exfiltration of payment and personal data to attacker-controlled infrastructure, constituting a severe supply chain attack.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user loads and interacts with a payment or subscription page containing the injected script.
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within the website's HTML, delivered via Picreel's compromised third-party script.
required_permissions: Access to the DOM (to read form fields and attach event listeners)
Network access to make outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches an event listener to the payment form's submit event, collects all form data including sensitive payment details, and sends this data via an HTTP POST request to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in exfiltration of user payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts form submissions and transmits the entire form data, including sensitive payment information, to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This behavior is indicative of web skimming and is not consistent with legitimate third-party scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate third-party marketing or analytics scripts should not access or transmit payment form data to unknown or untrusted domains. They are expected to operate within the scope of their advertised functionality and never exfiltrate sensitive user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may collect and transmit form data, but only to their own secure, vetted endpoints as part of authorized payment workflows. They do not send data to unrelated or untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Attaches event listeners to payment or subscription form submission events
Reads and serializes all form data, including payment fields
Sends outbound HTTP POST requests to hardcoded, non-affiliated domains
Script is injected via a compromised third-party supplier (supply chain vector)
No user consent or visible indication of data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: MageCart group compromises Picreel, a third-party web marketing supplier, by injecting malicious JavaScript into their codebase.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is present in Picreel's distributed scripts.

attack_chain.action: Compromised Picreel code is loaded by Forbes and other client websites as part of their normal third-party integrations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious MageCart script is executed in the context of the client websites, inheriting their trust and access.

attack_chain.action: MageCart script hooks into payment or subscription form submission events, collects sensitive user data, and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data from website users, enabling further fraud or resale.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to payment or subscription form submission events
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing form or payment data to domains not associated with the website or its payment processor
Unexpected modification or injection of scripts from third-party suppliers, especially those not previously present in the codebase
file_indicators: Injected or modified JavaScript code within website HTML, especially in <script> tags referencing third-party suppliers
References to external scripts loaded from compromised third-party domains (e.g., Picreel)
Presence of event listeners on sensitive forms (e.g., payment, subscription) that are not part of the original or expected codebase
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to domains not associated with the website or its legitimate payment processor
Network traffic to newly registered, suspicious, or known MageCart infrastructure domains
Unusual spikes in POST requests containing form data during user checkout or payment flows
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to payment or subscription forms and sends form data to external domains. Inspect third-party scripts for unauthorized modifications or unexpected code. Use network monitoring to detect POST requests containing sensitive data to untrusted or known malicious domains. Employ file integrity monitoring on web assets to detect unauthorized script injections or changes to third-party script references. Correlate behavioral, file, and network indicators to identify supply chain web skimming attacks.
